title: CRLA/143/2012 of SMT. VIMLA DEVI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 143 of 2012
Smt. Vimla Devi .............. Appellant

State of Uttarakhand and others .............. Respondents
Present: Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. Amit Bhatt, Deputy Advocate General (Criminal) assisted by
 Mr. V.P. Bahuguna, brief holder for the State/respondent No.1.
 Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
BARIN GHOSH, C.J. (Oral)
 A First Information Report was lodged by Vimla Devi
(PW1) at 11:00 A.M. of 13th December, 2009. In the F.I.R., it was
stated that at about 09:00 P.M. of 11th December, 2009 after having
had dinner, she, her children and her brother-in-law Heera Lal
(PW2) were sitting inside one of the rooms of her house when the
private respondents abusing PW1, PW2 and their family came in a
drunken condition, broke open the door and entered the house. It
was alleged that both the private respondents assaulted PW1 and
PW2 and respondent Bishan Singh tried to commit rape on her. It
was alleged that the private respondents, by using the name of the
caste to which PW1 and PW2 belong, tried to insult them and their
status as members of such caste. It was lastly stated that for the
reason as above, her husband and PW2 have been exposed to
further harm; so necessary action be taken. After the F.I.R. was
registered, PW1 and PW2 were taken to Dr. Rajesh Kumar Arya
(PW3) for their medical examination. PW3 examined PW1 and
found that she has received a lacerated wound injury below her left
eye and a contusion over her shoulder. PW1 reported that she is
having backache. That too was examined. PW3, then, prepared a
report and opined that each of those injuries were simple in nature

2
and have been caused by blunt substance. Upon examination of
PW2, PW3 noticed that he has received two contusions; one below
left eye and the other on left shoulder. Before PW3, PW2 also
reported that he has pain in stomach and shoulder. That complaint
was also taken note of. Having had done so, PW3 found that those
were caused by blunt substance and the injuries were simple in
nature. PW3 did not advice either PW1, or PW2 to take any
medical recourse. Soon thereafter, investigation was completed
and a charge-sheet was filed. On the basis thereof, charges were
framed. Respondent Bishan Singh was charged for commission of
offences punishable under Sections 323, 457, 504, 506 and 376/511
of I.P.C. as well as for offences punishable under Clauses (x) and
(xi) of sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Scheduled Castes and
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989; whereas
respondent Kundan Singh was charged for commission of offences
punishable under Sections 323, 457, 504 and 506 of I.P.C. as well
as for offences punishable under Clauses (x) and (xi) of sub-section
(1) of Section 3 of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. In order to prove the case of
the prosecution, three witnesses were called to give evidence.
Considering their evidence and other evidences brought on record,
by the judgment under appeal both Bishan Singh and Kundan Singh
have been acquitted of the charges. One of the reasons assigned
therefor appears to be that PW3, in course of tendering evidence,
stated that the injuries, as were found by him on PW1 and PW2,
were fresh, reddish and may have had been caused within 12 hours.
2. In the present appeal, it is being contended that having
had reported contusions in the examination report and having had
proved the contents thereof, PW3 could not hold out, in course of
answering questions to the court, that the contusions were fresh,
reddish and may have had been caused within 12 hours. The
learned counsel submitted that in the medical report proved by

3
PW3, contusions having been reported, which had indicated that the
bruises have become blue. In other words, it was suggested that
whenever it is reported that a person has received a contusion, the
same would signify that the skin has become blue. Dictionary
meaning of the word "contusion" is bruise. Medical meaning of the
word "contusion" is an injury in which the skin is not broken and
there is pain, swelling and discolouration. It is true that by passage
of time, the discolouration of the skin will make the skin blue, but
when it is reported that a person has received a contusion, that does
not signify that the contusion, as reported, has already turned the
skin in to blue. PW3 reported to the court that at the time when he
had seen PW1 and PW2, discolouration of the skin converted the
skin to red or reddish, inasmuch as, the same had taken place within
12 hours from the time he had examined the injuries. In course of
tendering evidence, PW1 held out that respondent Bishan Singh
tried to rape (Balatkaar) her. She did not say a word as to while
making such attempt, how respondent Bishan Singh acted. That
conduct on the part of PW1 also led to acquittal of the private
respondents. There is hardly any scope of interference with the
same, inasmuch as, statement to the effect "tried to rape" is no
evidence of trying to rape. In relation to offences pertaining to the
remaining Sections, under which the private respondents were
charged, neither PW1, nor PW2 held out that they were abused in
presence of any one else. At the same time, apart from a statement
that respondent Bishan Singh tried to rape PW1, there is no positive
statement on the part of either PW1 or PW2 as regards outraging
the modesty of PW1. The last aspect, as it appears to us, which
also prompted the court below to exonerate the private respondents,
is the evidence of PW1 to the effect that after the private
respondents broke open the door of the house of PW1, assaulted
PW1 and PW2 and respondent Bishan Singh tried to rape PW1;
PW2 left the house to fetch the husband of PW1 and the husband of
PW1, PW2 and the employer of PW1 returned to the house one

4
hour thereafter and, in the meantime, the private respondents
remained in the house of PW1 or in the house of the Gram Pradhan.
Considering the matters in the perspective of evidence, as was
brought on record by the prosecution, the court below has
exonerated the private respondents and we have not been able to
persuade ourselves to take a contrary view.
3. This appeal is not by the State. It is an appeal by the
victim. Despite having regard to the nature of evidence tendered by
the appellant before the court below, she has preferred this appeal
and, accordingly, has taken upon herself the entire responsibility
pertaining to the appeal. As a result of preferring this appeal,
private respondents as well as the Government had to be noticed
and they had to engage Advocates to defend their conduct
pertaining to the case. They have done so and, in consequence
thereof, they have incurred expenses. In a normal course, appellant
is liable to pay cost of the appeal for having lost therein. The
learned counsel appearing on behalf of the private respondents,
however, submitted that his clients are not insisting for payment of
cost. We accordingly, dismiss this appeal without cost.

4. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the court
below alongwith lower court records.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
 03.05.2013 03.05.2013
P. Singh
